- Model consistently overestimates prices, especially in the early part of the forecast horizon (first 10–15 days).
- Overshoots after sharp upward spikes in history (e.g., 82.21 → 83.26 → 86.29), then fails to correct downward.
- Underestimates prices in the final 5–10 days of the forecast, particularly when true values drop sharply (e.g., 88.54 → 72.54).
- Shows persistent bias toward higher values, suggesting a mean-reversion error — model doesn’t adjust downward enough after peaks.
- Lags in response to recent price drops; model often holds high forecasts even when history shows downward momentum.
- Overreacts to short-term volatility; forecasts spike higher than true values after minor price corrections.
- Tends to underestimate the magnitude of downward corrections, especially in the last 5–7 days of the forecast window.
